title: Seventeen Metres of Flag: the Carcassonne Clerk Who Filmed Argentina First
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Carcassonne, birth under the double walls
stops.date_confidence: attested; the Spanish, English and French encyclopedias agree exactly on day, month, year and town, and this is the single best-attested fact of his life
stops.campa: A son is born to the Py household in Carcassonne on the nineteenth of May, under the double walls of the Cité, in an Occitan town that has never seen a moving picture and will not see one in his childhood. The records agree on the day and on nothing else about these years: no school, no trade, no parents named, no explanation of where a boy from here learns lenses and chemistry. Whatever he learns, he learns somewhere the archives do not follow him. He will leave France in his twenties and never return, and the country that remembers his name is not this one.
suggested_refs: The walled Cité of Carcassonne, Aude, in the year of Py's birth

stops.name: Bordeaux, the presumed quay
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; no manifest, ship or port is named in any source, and the year is a placeholder inside the 'late 1880s' the encyclopedias give
stops.campa: No passenger list carries his name. Bordeaux stands here because it is the great French door onto the Río de la Plata in this decade, the quays where the South Atlantic steamers load emigrants for a republic advertising land and wages. A young man from Carcassonne bound for Buenos Aires most often leaves from here or from Marseille. Between the walled town of his birth and the port city that will make his name, every biography shows a blank, and the blank is the width of an ocean.
suggested_refs: The 1880s emigrant quays of Bordeaux and the South Atlantic steamer service to the Plate
sources: General knowledge of 1880s French to South American steamship routes; no Py-specific sailing record located

stops.name: Lisbon, the coaling call
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the stop is the shape of the standard route, not a documented call, and the date is an ordering placeholder
stops.campa: If the crossing runs the ordinary course, the ship puts in at Lisbon to coal and take on passengers before the long southward reach, and the emigrant from Carcassonne watches the Tagus widen under him for a day. Nothing in the record places him on these docks. The stop is entered because the alternative is to move a man from France to Argentina in one unexplained step, which is what the encyclopedias do, and because a crossing has ports whether or not anyone wrote them down.
suggested_refs: Period routing of Bordeaux to Buenos Aires steamers via Lisbon
sources: General knowledge of period transatlantic routing; no primary source for Py's crossing found

stops.name: Rio de Janeiro, the last port before the Plate
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; no source places Py aboard any named vessel, and the date is an ordering placeholder
stops.campa: The steamers for the Plate touch Rio before Montevideo and Buenos Aires, and any French passenger on that line sees the bay open between the mountains, the first tropical port of his life. Py's name attaches to no list here or anywhere on the water. The stop carries the shape of the voyage and no evidence of it. Somewhere on this run, in these years, a Frenchman with no trade anyone recorded is moving toward a country whose own pictures nobody has yet made.
suggested_refs: The Rio de Janeiro call on the French Line and Sud-Atlantique routes to the Plate
sources: General knowledge of period transatlantic routing; no primary source for Py's crossing found

stops.name: Buenos Aires, coming ashore on the Río de la Plata
stops.date_confidence: decade attested ('late 1880s' in the English and French articles); year, month, day, ship and season are all unrecorded
stops.campa: He comes ashore in the late eighteen eighties, one more Frenchman in a port swallowing Europe by the boatload. The city has photographers, gaslit theatres and litho presses, and no cinema, because there is not yet such a thing anywhere on earth. The sources agree on the decade and give no year and no vessel. Within ten years the machine that does not exist this year will be in his hands in a shop a few blocks from where he lands, and the first images of this country in motion will be his.
suggested_refs: The Buenos Aires waterfront in the decade of mass European arrival
sources: Wikipedia (English), 'Eugène Py', 'Py moved to Buenos Aires in the late 1880s'

stops.name: Casa Lepage, the counter at Bolívar 375
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; no source gives any year for Py joining the firm. All the record supports is 'before 1896'. The date here is an ordering device and the earlier 'c. 1888' and 'c. 1890' readings were inferred from Glücksmann's arrival, not from Py's
stops.campa: He takes work at Casa Lepage, the photographic supply house of the Belgian Henri Lepage, at Bolívar 375, nearly at the corner of Belgrano. It is a counter job: plates, chemicals, cameras sold to a city of amateurs. No source gives the year he starts, only that he is there before 1896, when the trade changes under him. The shop imports whatever Europe is making, which is how a clerk in Buenos Aires comes to hold new apparatus in his hands within months of Paris holding it.
stops.quote: calle Bolívar N° 375, casi esquina Belgrano
stops.quote_source: Wikipedia (Spanish), 'Eugenio Py', on the address of Casa Lepage
suggested_refs: The Casa Lepage building at Bolívar 375, Monserrat, Buenos Aires

stops.name: Casa Lepage, the Austrian at the next bench
stops.date_confidence: attested for Glücksmann ('llegó a Buenos Aires hacia 1890', starting as a photography assistant at about fifteen); the month is an ordering device
stops.campa: An Austrian boy of about fifteen, Max Glücksmann, is taken on at the same shop as a photography assistant. The two work the same rooms for eighteen years, the Frenchman at the apparatus and the younger man at the ledger. Nothing in the shop suggests which of them the century will favour. Glücksmann will buy the firm and build an exhibition business of a hundred halls in four countries; Py will keep the cameras, and end as the name on the first films rather than on any deed of sale.
suggested_refs: Max Glücksmann's beginnings as a photographic assistant at Casa Lepage

stops.name: Paris, the Cinématographe shown to a paying public
stops.date_confidence: general film history, carried in this dossier only as an inference; no source places Py in Paris at any point in his life and he is not present at this event
stops.campa: In a basement room on the boulevard des Capucines, at the end of December, the Lumière brothers show a paying public a machine that projects photographs in motion. Nothing about the invention is aimed at the Río de la Plata, and yet within seven months the same apparatus is crated, shipped and set up on a stage in Buenos Aires, with a clerk from Carcassonne sitting in the audience. It travels as freight, down the same steamer lines that bring plates and lenses to the shop where he works.
suggested_refs: The first paying public projection of the Lumière Cinématographe, Paris, December 1895
sources: Inferred from general film history; carried in the research pool as an inference, not as a documented Py fact

stops.name: Teatro Odeón, the first cinematograph in Argentina
stops.date_confidence: attested; the Spanish article on Argentine cinema and the French article on Py both give 28 July 1896, so the day can be stated firmly
stops.campa: In the Teatro Odeón on Esmeralda, almost at the corner of Corrientes, Francisco Pastor and Eustaquio Pellicer present the first cinematograph screenings Argentina has seen. Py is in the house with Lepage and Glücksmann, sent to look at the machine as stock: the shop sells apparatus, and this is apparatus. He watches other men's trains and workers and gardeners move on a sheet. Within a year he will stop watching imported pictures of Europe and point a camera at his own street.
stops.quote: se hicieron una serie de presentaciones el 28 de julio de 1896 en el Teatro Odeón
suggested_refs: The Teatro Odeón at Esmeralda 367, Buenos Aires, demolished in the twentieth century

stops.name: Casa Lepage, the Gaumont camera and the virgin stock
stops.date_confidence: year attested for the camera and the newly imported unexposed stock; the month is an ordering device and no source dates the shipment
stops.campa: The firm brings in a Gaumont camera and, for the first time, virgin film stock, unexposed and useless to anyone who cannot develop it. Until this shipment the trade in Buenos Aires runs one way: European reels arrive, are shown, and are sent on. Py takes the camera off the counter and carries it out of the shop. Nobody in the country has done this. Nobody in the country yet knows whether a picture shot here can be processed here, or whether the negative must cross the Atlantic twice to become an image.
suggested_refs: Gaumont camera equipment imported by Casa Lepage in 1897

stops.name: Plaza de Mayo, filming La bandera argentina
stops.date_confidence: year attested across all three encyclopedias; no month or day is recorded, and the January date is an ordering device
stops.campa: He sets the Gaumont in the Plaza de Mayo, before the Casa Rosada, and turns the crank on seventeen metres of film: the Argentine flag on its pole, moving in the wind, and nothing else. The first thing a camera does in this country is look at the flag Manuel Belgrano cut out of the sky's two colours eighty-five years earlier, and hold it. There is no plot, no actor, no scene. There is a piece of cloth that the republic agrees means the republic, and a Frenchman recording that it moves.
stops.quote: posiblemente la primera película filmada en Argentina
suggested_refs: The flagstaff of the Plaza de Mayo before the Casa Rosada, subject of the 1897 footage

stops.name: Casa Lepage, the first laboratory in the country
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the Spanish article, which ties the laboratory to the processing of the 1897 footage; month is an ordering device
stops.campa: To see what he has shot, the shop builds it: the first complete film laboratory in the country, developing, printing and titling in rooms that a decade before held only photographic plates. It is plumbing, trays and darkness and running water on Bolívar street. Until this year every reel shown in Argentina arrived finished from Europe; from this year a negative exposed in Buenos Aires can be printed a few doors from where it was exposed, and the country stops being only a market for other people's film.
stops.quote: la Casa Lepage instaló el primer laboratorio completo para procesar el material
suggested_refs: The Casa Lepage processing laboratory, first in Argentina

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the disputed first
stops.date_confidence: the dispute is real and undated; no source gives dates for Figner's earlier Buenos Aires views, so the year-end date is an ordering device placed after the flag film
stops.campa: The claim that follows him for a century is that this flag is the first film shot in Argentina. Later historians name an earlier hand: Federico Figner, born at Milevsko in Bohemia, an Austro-Hungarian subject, who had already made at least three short views of Buenos Aires. No dates for those views survive. So the founding shot of a national cinema is either Py's or a Bohemian phonograph dealer's, and the record does not close the question, though the country long ago chose which version to teach.
suggested_refs: The Figner priority claim, noted in French Wikipedia and unresolved in the Spanish and English accounts

stops.name: Salón Nacional, two hundred and fifty chairs on Maipú
stops.date_confidence: year attested with the street numbers and the seat count; no opening day is given, and Py's own involvement in the hall is nowhere stated
stops.campa: The Salón Nacional opens at Maipú 471, two hundred and fifty seats built to show films and nothing else, the first hall in Buenos Aires that is not a theatre lending its stage between other acts. Py's actualities and the imported reels Casa Lepage distributes now have a fixed address instead of a borrowed one. Whether he has any hand in the hall itself, no source says. From this year the city has somewhere purpose-made to put what he shoots, open every day and doing nothing else.
stops.quote: la primera sala cinematográfica de Buenos Aires, el Salón Nacional, ubicada en la calle Maipú 471/479
suggested_refs: The Salón Nacional at Maipú 471/479, capacity 250

segments.name: The Camera Turned on the State

stops.name: Casa Rosada, the visit of Campos Salles
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the month is unrecorded and the camera position is inferred from the nature of a state reception, not documented
stops.campa: The Brazilian president Manuel Ferraz de Campos Salles comes to Buenos Aires and Py films the visit: a reception between two young republics, recorded as it happens instead of engraved a month later for a magazine. It is called the first Argentine documentary. Three years earlier he had filmed cloth on a pole; now he is filming a head of state coming down onto a quay. After this the republic's public occasions are filmed as a matter of course, and the crank is turned by the man from the photographic shop.
suggested_refs: 'Visita del Dr Campos Salles a Buenos Aires' (1900), called the first Argentine documentary

stops.name: Dársena Norte, the review of the squadron
stops.date_confidence: year attested from the filmography list; no month, no quay and no vantage point are recorded, and the northern dock is a plausible siting rather than a documented one
stops.campa: He carries the camera to the northern docks for the review of the Argentine squadron, the navy's ships in line before the port and the crowd. The exact quay is not recorded. The habit is forming: whenever the state assembles itself in public, ships in review, presidents on gangways, generals at ceremonies, the Casa Lepage cameraman is somewhere at the edge with a tripod. No source names the fate of the print. Only the title and the year survive of what he shot that day.
suggested_refs: 'La Revista de la Escuadra Argentina' (1901)

stops.name: Museo Histórico Nacional, General Mitre among the relics
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the month is an ordering device. The museum's presence at Defensa 1600 since 1897 is separately attested
stops.campa: General Bartolomé Mitre, soldier, president, historian, walks through the Museo Histórico Nacional on Defensa street in San Telmo, and Py's camera walks with him. An old man of the independence generation moves among the relics of wars he helped to fight, filmed by the newest instrument of memory the country owns. The museum has stood at this address four years. Mitre has five years to live, and few men who fought the founding wars are left alive to be filmed walking anywhere.
suggested_refs: 'Visita del general Mitre al Museo Histórico' (1901); the museum at Defensa 1600, San Telmo

stops.name: Buenos Aires, sent across the Andes
stops.date_confidence: year attested; no month is given for the departure and the January date is an ordering device
stops.campa: Glücksmann decides that Py and a Spanish journalist, Enrique Casellas, will cross to the far side of the Andes and film the boundary quarrel with Chile. Py does not propose the trip. He is sent, the way a firm sends a technician. The frontier is being argued before Sir Thomas Holdich, commissioned by Edward the Seventh to mediate the arbitration, and the assignment is to bring back pictures of a dispute that two nations have agreed to settle by lawyers rather than by armies.
stops.quote: En 1902 Max Glücksmann decidió que Eugenio Py y un periodista español, Enrique Casellas, viajaran al país trasandino
suggested_refs: The 1902 Argentine-Chilean boundary arbitration and Sir Thomas Holdich's mediation

stops.name: Uspallata Pass, the road over the cordillera
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; no document describes Py's itinerary, and the pass is entered because it is the standard 1902 road from Mendoza to Santiago
stops.campa: The road from Mendoza to Santiago in this year runs through the Uspallata pass under Aconcagua, mule track and cart road, the corridor armies and pilgrims and traders have used for a century. No document describes his route. The pass stands here because it is the road, and because a man carrying a camera, a tripod and glass plates over that ground is doing something the flag in the Plaza de Mayo never asked of him. What he filmed on the way, if anything, is not known.
suggested_refs: The Uspallata pass, standard overland crossing between Mendoza and Santiago in 1902
sources: General knowledge of the 1902-era Mendoza to Santiago overland route; no Py-specific itinerary located

stops.name: Santiago de Chile, filming a border quarrel
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the Spanish source attests only that the pair travelled 'al país trasandino'. Nothing places Py in Santiago specifically, and no date within 1902 is given
stops.campa: He and Casellas cross into Chile with the equipment, a Spanish journalist to describe the frontier and a Frenchman to photograph it. Where the cameras were set up on the far side is stated nowhere: the trip is attested, its purpose is attested, and the shot list is gone. Within five years of the first Argentine film, a Buenos Aires firm is sending a cameraman over a mountain range to photograph a diplomatic question, on the calculation that the pictures will earn back the crossing from somebody paying at a door.
suggested_refs: The 1902 Chile assignment of Py and Enrique Casellas for Casa Lepage

segments.name: Sound, the Sale, and the Network

stops.name: Casa Lepage, the phonograph tied to the picture
stops.date_confidence: the starting year is attested ('desde 1907'); no month, no title and no venue are recorded, and the siting at the Bolívar workshop is inference
stops.campa: From this year he works at synchronising phonograph and picture, sound tied to image by machinery two decades before anyone makes it hold. No title from these experiments is named in any source, and no print is known to survive. Only the attempt is recorded, made in Buenos Aires by a man of forty-eight who had already put the first camera and the first laboratory in the country to work and now wants the picture to speak. Where in the city he tried it is not written down.
stops.quote: desde 1907 venía realizando las primeras experiencias de películas sonorizadas a partir de la sincronización fonográfica
suggested_refs: Py's phonographic synchronization experiments from 1907

stops.name: Casa Lepage, the house changes hands
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the Spanish articles on Py and on Glücksmann; no month or day is given
stops.campa: Henri Lepage sells the house to Max Glücksmann, the boy who came to the counter at fifteen and is now owner of the leading film business in the country. Eighteen years of shared workbench end with one of them holding the deed. What Py does after the sale is undocumented: no source states his employment, his wage or his title under the new owner. He is forty-nine years old, eleven years past the flag in the plaza, and the trade he opened here is now somebody's property.
suggested_refs: The 1908 sale of Casa Lepage to Max Glücksmann

stops.name: Montevideo, the network across the river
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the network's reach is attested but undated in stages, and nothing places Py himself on this bank of the Plate. The year is an ordering device
stops.campa: Glücksmann's exhibition business crosses the river: Buenos Aires, the interior of the country, Montevideo, and in time a hundred halls across Argentina, Chile, Uruguay and Paraguay. The actualities Py shot with a hand crank now circulate as inventory in a firm with branches. Nothing places Py himself on this bank of the Plate. The reach belongs to his work and not to his feet. His pictures cross the borders of four countries; he is not recorded as crossing the river.
suggested_refs: Glücksmann's exhibition network in Buenos Aires, the interior, and Montevideo

segments.name: The Gala and the Last Reels

stops.name: Teatro Colón, the premiere of Amalia
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the dedicated Spanish article on the film; the Spanish article on Py dates the film 1912 instead, and that reading is recorded rather than deleted
stops.campa: Amalia, drawn from José Mármol's novel of the Rosas terror, premieres at the Teatro Colón before President Victorino de la Plaza and his ministers. Enrique García Velloso directs and writes it; Py is listed under Fotografía. The cast is not professional: some eighty members of Buenos Aires society take the parts, Susana Larreta y Quintana as Amalia, José Miguens as Rosas, playing at a tyranny their grandparents survived. The takings go to a chapel and a school for girls.
suggested_refs: 'Amalia' (1914), produced by the Asociación del Divino Rostro, premiered at the Teatro Colón

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Mariano Moreno and the May Revolution
stops.date_confidence: year attested for the film; Py's participation is not. The film's own record names no cinematographer and does not mention him, while career summaries credit him with it
stops.campa: A silent life of Mariano Moreno, ideologue of the May Revolution, is made this year with Pablo Podestá in the title part and José Podestá as Saavedra, written and directed by García Velloso again. Whether Py stands behind the camera is not established. The film's own record names no cinematographer and does not mention him; the summaries of his career hand him the credit anyway. Nothing that survives of the production decides between the two, so both stand.
suggested_refs: 'Mariano Moreno y la Revolución de Mayo' (1915), directed and written by Enrique García Velloso
sources: Wikipedia (Spanish), 'Mariano Moreno y la Revolución de Mayo'

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the man who stepped into the shot
stops.date_confidence: unknown and contested. The English article gives no year; the '1901' formerly attached to this item was inferred from an adjacent filmography line and is withdrawn, since Santos-Dumont was in Paris that year. The Spanish biography of the aviator records no Argentine visit at all, and mentions Argentina only via a 1916 photograph with Eduardo Bradley, which is why 1916 is used here as a placeholder
stops.campa: Py films the aviator Alberto Santos Dumont, and the session produces what is remembered as the first sight gag in Argentine cinema: a man walks into the frame between camera and subject, refuses to move, and is finally removed by being spat in the face. Nothing records the year, the field or the occasion. The aviator's own biography mentions no Argentine visit at all. The gag survives as an anecdote while the footage, the date and the aerodrome do not.
suggested_refs: The undated Santos Dumont footage and the gag recorded in the Spanish account of Py

stops.name: Avenida Santa Fe, the Grand Splendid opens
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the opening; Py is not recorded as present, and the 'first cinema in Argentina' label attached to this hall collides with the same encyclopedia's claim for the Salón Nacional of 1900
stops.campa: Glücksmann opens the Grand Splendid on Avenida Santa Fe, a palace of a hall raised where a theatre and a carriage works had stood, and it is called the first cinema in Argentina by people who have forgotten the Salón Nacional of 1900 and its two hundred and fifty chairs. Py is sixty and is not recorded at the opening. The photographic counter on Bolívar street has become this in thirty years, and the man who first carried a camera out of that counter is on no invitation list anyone preserved.
stops.quote: la primera sala de cine de Argentina
stops.quote_source: Wikipedia (Spanish), 'Max Glücksmann', on the Grand Splendid
suggested_refs: The Grand Splendid at Avenida Santa Fe 1860, opened 14 May 1919

stops.name: San Martín, the death in the suburb
stops.date_confidence: attested; all three encyclopedias agree on the day, the town and the age of sixty-five. The street, the house and the cause are unrecorded
stops.campa: He dies on the twenty-sixth of August at San Martín, a factory suburb north-west of the capital, sixty-five years old. By this year Argentine cinema has features, studios, stars and a distribution trade worth fortunes, and none of it is his. No source gives the street, the house or the cause. He came ashore here as a young man in a country that had no cinema and no word for one, and he leaves a country that has both, with the last nine years of his own life unrecorded by anybody.
suggested_refs: Ciudad del Libertador General San Martín, Partido de General San Martín, Buenos Aires Province

segments.name: What Is Kept and What Is Not

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the grave nobody records
stops.date_confidence: gap, not a date. No burial record of any kind was located; the date is placed two days after the death purely to order the stop, and the pin is the city's general marker rather than any cemetery
stops.campa: No cemetery, no plot, no stone. Nothing consulted names where the body of the man who shot the first Argentine film was put, and the plausible guesses, Chacarita, Recoleta, a parish ground in San Martín, are guesses and are refused here rather than written down as facts. A country that keeps its founders in marble has mislaid this one entirely. The films are catalogued by title and year; the grave has no entry anywhere, and nobody now alive was ever told where to look.
suggested_refs: No burial record located in any consulted source; a gap for a future archival pass
sources: Gap: absent from Spanish, English and French Wikipedia; web search exhausted without a usable result

stops.name: Carcassonne, nothing on the French side
stops.date_confidence: gap. No memorial, plaque, repatriation of remains or French commemoration was located in any source; the date is an ordering device set after the death
stops.campa: In the town of his birth there is nothing. No plaque on a wall, no return of remains, no street, no notice that a man from here pointed the first camera at a South American republic and stayed twenty years to film it. France made the machine and the man, and remembers only the machine. Sixty-five years and one ocean lie between the birthplace and the death, and neither shore has raised anything to join the two ends of him. No source consulted mentions this town in connection with him at all, and the silence is entered as silence.
suggested_refs: Absence of any Carcassonne memorial to Py; noted as a gap across all consulted sources
sources: Absence noted across Spanish, English and French Wikipedia; no memorial or repatriation record located

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the two books that hold the name
stops.date_confidence: attested for the publication years, 1966 for Mahieu and 1998 for Di Núbila's first volume; the stop is dated to the earlier of the two
stops.campa: What holds the name in place is not stone but two histories in Spanish: José Agustín Mahieu's Breve historia del cine argentino of 1966, and Domingo Di Núbila's Historia del cine argentino, whose first volume is called the golden age. Neither is indicated as translated into any other language. So the founding cameraman of a national cinema is legible in full only to readers of the country that mislaid his grave. Outside Spanish he is three encyclopedia entries that disagree with each other.
suggested_refs: Mahieu, Breve historia del cine argentino (1966); Di Núbila, Historia del cine argentino I, La época de oro (1998)

stops.name: Bolívar 375, the plaque on the wall
stops.date_confidence: undated. No source gives the year the marker was placed; the date is an ordering device only, set at the centenary of the 1897 filming and carrying no claim about the plaque itself
stops.campa: The building at Bolívar 375 still stands, and on its wall is a plaque saying what happened inside it: the shop where Py, Lepage and Glücksmann worked, where the first film camera and the first laboratory in the country were kept. It is the one physical marker anyone has found for him. No statue, no museum room, no street. A brass rectangle at head height on a downtown facade, read by nobody in particular, is the whole monument to the beginning of Argentine cinema.
suggested_refs: The commemorative plaque on the former Casa Lepage building, Bolívar 375
